title: Chimera: Communication Fusion for Hybrid Parallelism in Large Language Models
problem: Hybrid parallelism strategies (tensor, pipeline, sequence, data parallelism combined) for LLM training and inference on multi-NPU systems generate a large volume of diverse collective communications whose blocking nature severely throttles compute utilization. Redundant communication operators introduced by combining multiple parallelism dimensions compound this bottleneck.
method: Chimera performs a systematic analysis of communication processes for each parallelism dimension (tensor, pipeline, data, sequence), identifies redundant collective operations that arise when multiple parallelism strategies are combined, and eliminates them by fusing adjacent communication operators during parallelism transformation. It reorders operations and generates a single redundancy-free communication operator that achieves the semantics of the original multi-collective sequence. The resulting fused operator is injected into the LLM computation graph as a replacement for the original blocking collectives.

title: OptiPIM: Optimizing Processing-in-Memory Acceleration Using Integer Linear Programming
problem: Efficient PIM acceleration requires precise software-hardware mapping that transforms application algorithms into PIM operations and data layouts, but existing PIM accelerators rely on manually tuned heuristics or exhaustive search, producing under-optimized mappings and/or prohibitively long optimization times.
method: OptiPIM formulates the PIM mapping problem as an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) problem using a PIM-friendly mapping representation with accurate cost modeling that concisely covers the entire design space. The framework is implemented as a compiler pass inside the open-source MLIR framework, enabling it to consume PyTorch workloads and emit optimized mappings for PIM accelerators. OptiPIM generates optimal mappings within 4 minutes by exploiting the problem structure to make the ILP tractable.

title: AiF: Accelerating On-Device LLM Inference Using In-Flash Processing
problem: On-device LLM inference with SSD offloading is severely bottlenecked by the limited external read bandwidth of flash storage (NAND-to-host path), making inference latency unacceptably high even though LLM weight matrices fit in flash capacity. Existing SSD offloading engines are bound by PCIe/interface bandwidth rather than the high internal NAND bandwidth.
method: AiF integrates matrix-vector multiplication (GEMV) compute units directly inside flash chips (Accelerator-in-Flash), exploiting the high internal NAND plane-level bandwidth without routing data across the external interface. Two novel flash read techniques are introduced specifically for LLM weight access patterns stored in flash memory. AiF also employs a streamlined error correction process that delivers a 4x boost in internal read bandwidth with minimal overhead, enabling in-flash GEMV operations to run at near-full internal bandwidth.

title: TetrisLock: Quantum Circuit Split Compilation with Interlocking Patterns
problem: Untrusted quantum compilers can steal circuit intellectual property (IP) and reverse-engineer proprietary quantum algorithms.
method: TetrisLock splits quantum circuits into two interdependent segments with interlocking patterns; original functionality only recoverable by combining both segments; neither segment alone reveals the complete circuit structure; eliminates need for trusted compiler on random circuits.

title: HH-PIM: Dynamic Optimization of Power and Performance with Heterogeneous-Hybrid PIM for Edge AI Devices
problem: Efficient PIM architectures for edge AI devices face trade-offs: traditional PIM reduces data movement but has continuous power demands; hybrid PIM with nonvolatile memory (MRAM/ReRAM) reduces power but has mismatch between fixed computing resources and dynamically changing inference workloads.
method: Heterogeneous-Hybrid PIM (HH-PIM) architecture with two heterogeneous compute modules: (1) high-performance MRAM-SRAM PIM modules, (2) low-power MRAM-SRAM PIM modules. Data placement optimization algorithm dynamically allocates data based on computational demand to maximize energy efficiency while meeting latency constraints.

title: Ariadne: A Hotness-Aware and Size-Adaptive Compressed Swap Technique for Fast Application Relaunch and Reduced CPU Usage on Mobile Devices
problem: Mobile devices under memory pressure use ZRAM (RAM-based compressed swap) to defer app eviction, but ZRAM prolongs relaunch latency and wastes CPU time because it applies uniform compression settings regardless of data hotness, does not differentiate compression chunk size, and lacks prefetching of soon-to-be-needed decompressed data.
method: Ariadne introduces three coordinated techniques: (1) a low-overhead hotness-aware data organization scheme that classifies anonymous memory pages as hot, warm, or cold based on observed relaunch access patterns, allowing reuse of hotness labels across consecutive relaunches; (2) a size-adaptive compression scheme that uses small chunk sizes for hot/warm data (enabling fast decompression on the critical relaunch path) and large chunk sizes for cold data (improving compression ratio); and (3) a proactive decompression scheme that predicts the next set of pages needed during relaunch and decompresses them in advance to overlap decompression with computation.

title: Panacea: Novel DNN Accelerator using Accuracy-Preserving Asymmetric Quantization and Energy-Saving Bit-Slice Sparsity
problem: Symmetric quantization introduces unacceptable accuracy loss for large-scale DNNs due to asymmetric activation distributions, but existing asymmetric quantization schemes produce many nonzero bit-slices that cannot be exploited by bit-slice GEMM accelerators designed for symmetric (zero-heavy) representations.
method: Panacea introduces Asymmetrically-Quantized bit-Slice GEMM (AQS-GEMM), which compresses frequent nonzero slices generated by asymmetric quantization and skips their computation. Two algorithm-hardware co-optimization techniques increase slice-level sparsity: zero-point manipulation (adjusting quantization zero points to shift frequent values toward zero) and distribution-based bit-slicing (selecting bit-slices that maximize sparsity based on activation distribution). Panacea's dataflow is specialized for sparse/dense mixed workloads on tiled AQS-GEMM, with run-length encoding to maximize data reuse and minimize off-chip memory traffic.

title: Caravan: A Hardware/Software Co-Design for Efficient SIMD Neighbor Search on Point Clouds
problem: Neighbor search in 3D point cloud processing via k-d trees is compute-intensive and exhibits SIMD underutilization: consecutive queries follow similar tree paths but diverge at deeper levels, causing sparse VPU lane usage that standard SIMD instructions cannot efficiently handle.
method: Caravan-SW batches consecutive neighbor search queries that visit similar k-d tree nodes and processes them in parallel using SIMD (AVX512) instructions. At deeper tree levels where query navigation diverges, Caravan-HW adds two new ISA instructions that enable re-indexing of valid (non-empty) SIMD lanes and fast operand shuffling, allowing dense SIMD operations on the remaining active lanes. The hardware modification is lightweight, requiring only 0.032 mm2 of additional silicon area.

title: An Energy-Efficient Kalman Filter Architecture with Tunable Accuracy for Brain-Computer Interfaces
problem: Kalman Filters are standard for BCIs to predict motion from brain activity, but hardware implementations specialized for embedded BCI constraints (latency-accuracy tuning, energy efficiency) are lacking.
method: A configurable KF hardware architecture with tunable latency and accuracy parameters enables design-space exploration for BCI applications; integrated as accelerators into a heterogeneous SoC, supporting efficient neural data processing with dynamic parameter adjustment.

title: Late Breaking Results: Source-Aware Adaptive Cache Management for CXL-enabled Disaggregated Memory Sharing
problem: CXL-enabled disaggregated memory systems with multiple hosts exhibit changing access patterns; conventional cache policies cannot track per-host behavior, making it difficult to optimize shared memory efficiency.
method: Alchemy system jointly optimizes cache replacement and bypassing policies using reinforcement learning with source-aware adaptivity. It runs as an online RL agent that tracks per-host access patterns. Rewards derive from sampling-based action effectiveness and per-host macro-level performance metrics.

title: Forecasting GPU Performance for Deep Learning Training and Inference
problem: Predicting GPU performance for deep learning workloads on unseen GPU models (new GPU on existing model, or existing model on new GPU) is inaccurate with prior ML-based approaches, which attempt to predict end-to-end kernel latency directly and suffer >100% error on new model-GPU pairs.
method: NeuSight decomposes a single DL kernel prediction into smaller working sets called 'tiles' that correspond to the GPU's SM-level execution granularity. Tile-granularity predictions are made by a learned ML model, then aggregated across tiles to estimate end-to-end latency. The approach is bounded by fundamental performance laws (roofline model) and incorporates both GPU hardware parameters and software library optimizations (cuDNN, cuBLAS heuristics) to constrain the prediction space, enabling generalization to unseen GPUs by parameterizing hardware characteristics rather than encoding GPU identity.

title: 24.3: A PVT-Robust 2×Interleaved 2.2GS/s ADC with Gated-CCRO-Based Quantizer Shared Across Channels and Steps Achieving >4.5GHz ERBW
problem: Ring-oscillator (RO)-based ADCs offer compact, scaling-friendly designs but face challenges: VC-RO requires nonlinear tuning calibration and individual ROs per sub-channel; gated-RO shares poorly across channels due to long integer-counting; cyclic coupled ROs have phase errors. Achieving high energy/area efficiency with multi-channel interleaving remains difficult.
method: A 2×64-channel time-interleaved two-step ADC uses a gated cyclic coupled ring-oscillator (G-CCRO) based quantizer shared across both channels and conversion steps. The G-CCRO operates independently of sampled input amplitude with inherent phase interpolation, while the ramp generator is reallocated to the reference path (vs. input path) to maintain constant input impedance and reduce kickback.

title: Criticality-Aware Instruction-Centric Bandwidth Partitioning for Data Center Applications
problem: Co-locating latency-critical (LC) and best-effort (BE) tasks on shared datacenter nodes causes memory bandwidth contention that results in priority inversion, where BE tasks monopolize bandwidth and cause LC tasks to violate quality-of-service (QoS) requirements.
method: Pivot is a bandwidth partitioning system that prioritizes LC memory accesses at every component along the full memory path (L1/L2/L3 caches, DRAM controller) rather than at a single bottleneck point. Critically, Pivot selectively prioritizes only performance-critical loads—those causing long stalls on the re-order buffer (ROB)—rather than all LC accesses. A two-phase profiling technique identifies these critical loads offline with minimal runtime overhead: Phase 1 profiles whole-execution hit/miss behavior per load PC, and Phase 2 uses those profiles to tag critical loads for hardware prioritization during production runs.

title: SWIPER: Minimizing Fault-Tolerant Quantum Program Latency via Speculative Window Decoding
problem: Parallel window decoding for fault-tolerant quantum error correction requires some decoding tasks to be delayed until preceding windows complete, creating head-of-line blocking that inflates program runtime, especially during T gate teleportation where decoding latency directly extends logical circuit depth.
method: SWIPER introduces a speculative window decoder inspired by classical branch prediction. A lightweight speculation step predicts data dependencies between adjacent decoding windows, allowing multiple layers of decoding tasks to begin simultaneously rather than waiting for dependency resolution. If speculation is wrong, the decoder rolls back and re-decodes; the state-of-the-art compilation pipeline ensures that speculation opportunities are maximized. Performance is evaluated using a detailed open-source cycle-accurate simulator.

title: All-in-Memory Stochastic Computing using ReRAM
problem: Stochastic computing bit-stream generators consume over 80% of system power and area; current solutions focus on gate optimization but ignore high data movement costs between memory and processor for bit-stream exchange.
method: All-in-memory stochastic computing leverages ReRAM physics to: (1) generate low-cost true random numbers and stochastic bit-streams in-place, (2) perform SC operations directly on ReRAM cells, and (3) convert bit-streams back to binary. ReRAM's robustness to errors complements SC's fault tolerance.

title: Mascot: Predicting Memory Dependencies and Opportunities for Speculative Memory Bypassing
problem: Memory dependence prediction (MDP) and speculative memory bypassing (SMB) require conflicting predictor properties: MDP tolerates false positives but not false negatives, while SMB tolerates false negatives but not false positives. Prior TAGE-based predictors for either mechanism fail to learn patterns of non-dependence, causing inaccuracy.
method: Mascot is a TAGE-inspired predictor that learns both dependence and non-dependence contexts. Unlike prior designs that only learn dependence patterns, Mascot tracks the history of non-aliasing outcomes in the TAGE table entries, enabling low false negative rates required for MDP and low false positive rates required for SMB from a single shared structure. The predictor is used in two modes: MDP-only (for load issue gating) and combined MDP+SMB (for value forwarding from store to load bypassing address resolution).
